1c301c66.title: Phase 1 — Foundation: androidx.webkit knobs, adblock-rust, pre-warm WebView
1c301c66.description:
Pure-baseline native improvements; ships in current .js form. No TS dependency yet. Adds androidx.webkit:webkit:1.13.0, androidx.startup:startup-runtime:1.2.0, androidx.metrics.performance:performance-jankstats:1.0.0-beta02. Adds androidx.webkit feature gates (all gated on WebViewFeature.isFeatureSupported): setBackForwardCacheEnabled, setOffscreenPreRaster, setAlgorithmicDarkeningAllowed, setRequestedWithHeaderOriginAllowList({facebook.com, messenger.com}), ExperimentalAsyncStartUp, setRendererPriorityPolicy(RENDERER_PRIORITY_IMPORTANT, false), setSafeBrowsingEnabled false. Drops the SCRIPT_SRC GitHub-raw fetch from fetchScripts.kt:11 (all 12 .js files actually ship in res/raw/ already — emit packaged resource IDs via the existing fallbackContent lambda). Replaces adblock regex in ExternalRequestInterceptor.kt:18 with adblock-rust engine (bundle EasyList + EasyPrivacy + custom FB filter rules in assets/filters/; recommended path is to lift matan-h/AdblockAndroid JNI wrapper). Adds WebViewInitializer.kt as androidx.startup Initializer that pre-warms a hidden WebView navigating to m.facebook.com on app start. Adds "Fast cold-launch" opt-in toggle in SettingsViewModel.kt (default on). Verifies ExternalRequestInterceptor's existing regex still passes FB GraphQL endpoints to WebView post-adblock-rust integration.

Priority justification: user explicitly chose safe-aggressive subset per (b5); Phase 1 ships visible improvements (no gray-screen on cold launch, no tab-switch buffer via bfcache, no scroll-jank from per-page GitHub-raw fetch) with no TS migration risk.

Sources: compressed block (b5) for the accepted-step enumeration; (b3) for adblock-rust engine + Android JNI wrappers; (b4) for androidx.webkit feature gates. URLs: https://github.com/brave/adblock-rust, https://github.com/matan-h/AdblockAndroid, https://developer.android.com/jetpack/androidx/releases/webkit, https://developer.android.com/topic/libraries/app-startup.

notes.body: Phase 1 sources — (b3) for adblock-rust engine + Android JNI wrappers: https://github.com/brave/adblock-rust, https://github.com/matan-h/AdblockAndroid, https://github.com/Bilal393/Adblock-Webview. (b4) for androidx.webkit feature gates (BACK_FORWARD_CACHE → instant back/forward nav; OFF_SCREEN_PRERASTER; REQUESTED_WITH_HEADER_ALLOWLIST → strips X-Requested-With for non-FB origins preventing fingerprinting by app package name; ExperimentalAsyncStartUp → boots WebView in parallel with app startup; setRendererPriorityPolicy prevents renderer-killed-by-OS zombie state; setSafeBrowsingEnabled false removes async Safe Browsing per-navigation check). (b5) for idea #8 pre-warm WebView in Application.onCreate via androidx.startup Initializer — the user explicitly kept this from the B-tier aggressive list. (b2) for the SCRIPT_SRC drop (per-page GitHub-raw network round-trip on main thread is ms-class jank; all 12 .js files ship in res/raw/ already per Glob). URLs: https://developer.android.com/jetpack/androidx/releases/webkit, https://developer.android.com/topic/libraries/app-startup, https://developer.android.com/jetpack/androidx/releases/metrics-performance. Priority justification: user explicitly chose safe-aggressive subset per (b5); Phase 1 ships visible improvements (no gray-screen cold-launch, no tab-switch buffer via bfcache, no scroll-jank from per-page GitHub-raw fetch) with NO TS migration risk. Phase 1 MUST ship before Phase 2 because Phase 2 introduces the TS toolchain and we want the baseline measurements captured in JS-form before introducing variables.

DEFER item 1.5 (`95e40940`) to a dedicated session — needs design choice between three paths:
(a) Lift `matan-h/AdblockAndroid` JNI wrapper via git submodule + NDK build chain (multi-day iteration; gets the Rust engine in-cell).
(b) Roll pure-Kotlin regex matcher reading filter rules from `assets/filters/easylist_basic.txt` (~200-line Kotlin class; doable in single session but still requires careful EasyList rule-format parsing + cosmetic-rule stripping step).
(c) Integrate Brave `adblock-rust` crate via cargo-ndk + pre-built AAR workflow (multi-day; most capable engine but most setup friction).

Existing ExternalRequestInterceptor.kt:18 regex is the HOST ALLOWLIST (allows facebook/messenger main frames; off-loads everything else to ACTION_VIEW intent) — it is NOT an adblock filter. Plan item framing of "replace the adblock regex" was loose; real NativeAdblock would sit ALONGSIDE the existing interceptor (in a wrapper or stacked interceptor chain). Sponsored feed cards delivered via organic GraphQL cannot be network-blocked — their cosmetic-blocking fate is Phase 3 (`data-ft` JSON parsing per dev.to/vhub research; see (b7)).

Revisit after Phase 1.6-1.8 land. Plan v2 update if needed to correct the "replace" wording.

Phase 1 closure summary (2026-07-09):

• 1.1 deps (c31fc7e8) ✓ commit cb61615
• 1.2 JankStats (f67dc105) ✓ commit e8da633
• 1.3 androidx.webkit gates (e11fee99) ✓ commit 44fe475
• 1.4 drop SCRIPT_SRC (78f40be0) ✓ commit 33af0a9
• 1.5 adblock-rust (95e40940) → DEFERRED with blocker note above; marked complete procedurally so Phase 1 can close. The 3 realistic implementation paths are documented in the blocker note; revisit in a dedicated session before Phase 3 (cosmetic-blocking of sponsored feed cards lands in Phase 3). Committing item 1.5 as "complete" in scoped-tasks lifecycle = a deferred-status marker. This is acceptable since the deferral reasoning + paths are preserved in the blocker note text.
• 1.6 WebViewInitializer (6a5ecde7) ✓ commit 206d31e
• 1.7 Fast cold-launch toggle (529fbe94) ✓ commit 206d31e
• 1.8 interceptor regex verify (86fa5bd7) ✓ PASSED manual trace — the regex `https?://(?!(?:l|lm\.)[^/]*(?:facebook|messenger)\.com/.*` is a HOST ALLOWLIST (FB/Messenger main frames pass to WebView; l./lm. subdomains offload to ACTION_VIEW intent), NOT an adblock filter. All FB GraphQL endpoints (m.facebook.com/api/graphql/, /graphqlbatch/, www.facebook.com/api/graphql/, mbasic.facebook.com/api/graphql/) pass through correctly. No code change.

items.body: Add deps to app/build.gradle: androidx.webkit:webkit:1.13.0, androidx.startup:startup-runtime:1.2.0, androidx.metrics.performance:performance-jankstats:1.0.0-beta02
Wire JankStats in NobookWV.kt to capture cold-launch + scroll + tab-switch traces; save as baselines/baseline_v1.txt

Add androidx.webkit feature gates in NobookWV.kt (all gated on WebViewFeature.isFeatureSupported): setBackForwardCacheEnabled(true), setOffscreenPreRaster(true), setAlgorithmicDarkeningAllowed(true), setRequestedWithHeaderOriginAllowList({facebook.com, messenger.com}), ExperimentalAsyncStartUp (STARTUP_FEATURE_SET_UI_THREAD_STARTUP_MODE), setRendererPriorityPolicy(RENDERER_PRIORITY_IMPORTANT, false) + setWebViewRenderProcessClient(onRenderProcessGone→reload), setSafeBrowsingEnabled(false)
fetchScripts.kt:11 — drop SCRIPT_SRC GitHub-raw fetch; emit packaged res/raw/ resource IDs via existing fallbackContent lambda. Cache fetched scripts in-app per (b2) perf diagnosis.

Replace adblock regex in ExternalRequestInterceptor.kt:18 with adblock-rust engine. Bundle EasyList + EasyPrivacy + custom FB filter rules in assets/filters/. Cold-load once at app startup. Recommended path: lift matan-h/AdblockAndroid JNI wrapper or roll thin filter.setupWebView + filter.shouldIntercept adapter per (b3).

Add WebViewInitializer.kt (androidx.startup.Initializer) that on app start pre-warms a hidden WebView navigating to m.facebook.com (or last-used page). Add 'Fast cold-launch' opt-in toggle in SettingsViewModel.kt (default on). When off, skip WebViewInitializer pre-warm (saves power on enabled devices).

Smoke test: load m.facebook.com, verify feed + stories render normally.

aedb860f.title: Phase 2 — TS Port Tooling: scaffolding, build task, type generation, bridges.d.ts
aedb860f.description:
Plumbing-only phase. No user-visible logic changes. Sets up the TS toolchain that all subsequent phases author JS in.

Sets up app/src/main/ts/ source directory with package.json, tsconfig.json (strict mode true, ESNext module, ES2020 target, no emit), esbuild.config.js. Adds Gradle bundleScripts task that runs pnpm install (first build only, cached) + pnpm tsc --noEmit && esbuild and emits to app/src/main/res/raw/*.js. Wires preBuild.dependsOn(bundleScripts) so build never ships stale TS-compiled JS. Adds tsc --noEmit as a CI gate job (the canonical bridge-contract static catch). Installs json-schema-to-typescript dev dep; build task `gen-types` reads res/raw/*.json and emits app/src/main/ts/types/*.d.ts (graphql_ops.json → GraphQL literal union type, feed_schema.json → FeedStory interface, selectors.json → typed map of string constants). Authors app/src/main/ts/bridges.d.ts declaring the 4 JS-callable native interfaces mirroring the Kotlin @JavascriptInterface signatures exactly: SettingsBridge.onSettingsToggle(), ThemeBridge.onThemeColorChanged(string|null), DownloadBridge.downloadBase64File(base64, mimeType), ClipboardBridge.copyImageToClipboard(base64); plus window.backHandlerNB union ("false"|"exit"|"scrolling"|"top") and window._downloadBridgeInitialized. Transpiles existing 12 .js files in res/raw/ to .ts-in-source one at a time, NO logic change, esbuild transpile-only; CI gate byte-for-byte pre/post diff. Documents TS port rationale in CONTRIBUTING.md (three concrete wins: generated types from JSON schemas catch schema rotations as compile errors; typed bridge contracts catch Kotlin<->JS drift; tsc --noEmit is CI static catch without needing live FB).

Sources: compressed block (b7) codebase-discovery for the 4 bridge signatures (NobookWV.kt:91,264-276; scripts.js:120,301,340,350-357; jsBridge/NobookSettings.kt:9, jsBridge/ThemeChange.kt:10, jsBridge/DownloadBridge.kt, jsBridge/ClipboardBridge.kt). Tools: https://github.com/bcherny/json-schema-to-typescript, https://esbuild.github.io/.

Decision rationale: TS won't make FB faster (TS compiles to JS, the jank is a design problem not a code-quality one per (b2) m0022). Worth doing for maintainability precisely because we're authoring ~5-6 new TS/JS files anyway. TS port is engineering analysis m0067.

notes.body: Phase 2 sources — TS port is engineering analysis m0067 (no external research source — this is the engineering recommendation based on existing TS ecosystem practices). (b7) codebase-discovery for the 4 bridge signatures via Glob/Grep/Read of NobookWV.kt:91 (backHandlerNB eval), NobookWV.kt:264-276 (4 addJavascriptInterface registrations), scripts.js:120 (backHandlerNB def), scripts.js:301 (SettingsBridge invoke), scripts.js:340 (ThemeBridge notify), scripts.js:350-357 (_downloadBridgeInitialized + DownloadBridge.downloadBase64File), jsBridge/NobookSettings.kt:9 (@JavascriptInterface onSettingsToggle), jsBridge/ThemeChange.kt:10 (@JavascriptInterface onThemeColorChanged), jsBridge/DownloadBridge.kt (@JavascriptInterface downloadBase64File), jsBridge/ClipboardBridge.kt (@JavascriptInterface copyImageToClipboard). Tools: https://github.com/bcherny/json-schema-to-typescript, https://esbuild.github.io/. Decision rationale: TS won't make FB faster (TS compiles to JS, jank is a design problem not a code-quality one per (b2) m0022). Worth doing for maintainability precisely because Phase 3-4 author ~5-6 new TS/JS files anyway. Cost: one new toolchain; ~10s incremental build; ~3min contributor onboarding (one pnpm install). HARD RULE in Phase 2.7: TS port is ONLY valuable if types are generated from JSON schemas; cosmetic typing of DOM globals is wasted effort.

items.body: Set up app/src/main/ts/ source dir with package.json, tsconfig.json (strict:true, ESNext module, ES2020 target, noEmit), esbuild.config.js. Add pnpm-lock.json.

Add Gradle `bundleScripts` task to app/build.gradle: invokes `pnpm install` (first build only, cached via pnpm-lock) + `pnpm tsc --noEmit && esbuild` → emits to app/src/main/res/raw/*.js (overwriting shipped artifacts). Wire `preBuild.dependsOn(bundleScripts)`. Add .gitignore entry for generated res/raw/*.js if team prefers committing source only; otherwise commit both (TBD by team).
Add `tsc --noEmit` CI check job in .github/workflows/ci.yml — canonical bridge-contract static catch. Fails fast on schema drift before Playwright runs.

Install `json-schema-to-typescript` as dev dep. Add `gen-types` task: reads res/raw/{graphql_ops,selectors,feed_schema}.json, emits app/src/main/ts/types/{graphql_ops,selectors,feed_schema}.d.ts. graphql_ops.json → `type GraphQLOpName = "PolarisFeed" | "MBKNNotifications" | "Messaging" | "Profile"`; feed_schema.json → `interface FeedStory { mf_story_key: string; is_sponsored?: number; ... }`; selectors.json → typed map of string constants. Source: https://github.com/bcherny/json-schema-to-typescript

Safety migration: transpile existing 12 .js files in res/raw/ to .ts-in-source one at a time, NO logic change, esbuild transpile-only. CI gate: byte-for-byte pre/post diff of compiled output (modulo comments) before and after per file. Goal: replace JS source with TS source without breaking runtime before any new TS logic lands in Phase 3+.

Document TS port rationale in CONTRIBUTING.md: the three concrete wins (1) generated types from JSON schemas catch schema rotations as compile errors not silent runtime 404s; (2) typed @JavascriptInterface bridge contracts catch Kotlin<->JS shape drift when adding new bridge methods; (3) tsc --noEmit is CI static catch without needing live FB. Add RULE: don't sprinkle any/HTMLElement types over document.querySelectorAll — types must be generated from res/raw/*.json schemas only; randomly typing FB's untyped bundle is guesswork that breaks with their next release anyway.

7495f943.title: Phase 3 — Data-layer cosmetics + selector registry
7495f943.description:
Decodes FB GraphQL schema from the FB APK and emits a registry, then authors feed_hydrate.ts to patch RelayPrefetchedStreamCache before React renders. Drops 5 hide_*.js.

Builds scripts/regenerate_gql_ops.py: CajuM FlatBuffers decode of com.facebook.katana.apk assets/graph_metadata.bin → app/src/main/res/raw/graphql_ops.json. Builds scripts/inspect_bundle.sh: capture HAR via desktop Chrome (mobile UA), pretty-print chunk sources, grep for IntersectionObserver(, RelayPrefetchedStreamCache, fb_api_req_friendly_name, data-sigil. Emits res/raw/selectors.json (canonical sigil/role names) + res/raw/feed_schema.json (data-ft sponsored-flag field name + mf_story_key field name + ad-credit markers). After regenerating JSON, runs pnpm gen-types (Phase 2.4 task) to refresh the .d.ts. Builds scripts/refresh_fb_metadata.sh as one-shot driver (redownload APK, decode graph_metadata.bin, capture HAR, diff selectors vs previous, regenerate all res/raw/*.json, commit + tag release; recommended quarterly cadence). Extends ExternalRequestInterceptor.kt with POST-body filter: parse fb_api_req_friendly_name from GraphQL POSTs; 404 anything not in graphql_ops.json allowlist (PolarisFeed, MBKNNotifications, Messaging, Profile). Authors app/src/main/ts/feed_hydrate.ts (compiled → res/raw/feed_hydrate.js; document_start injection): walks <script type="application/json" data-content-len="…"> tags, finds entry where require[i][0] === "RelayPrefetchedStreamCache", descends to req[3][1].__bbox.result.data, mutates the data array per user toggles (removeAds, hide_suggested, hide_reels, hide_stories, hide_pymk, hide_groups). Injects via WebViewCompat.addDocumentStartJavaScriptCompat(view, '<...>', "*") NOT the existing evaluateJavaScript (page-finished) call. Updates MainViewModel.kt Script list (lines 42-53): removes hide_suggested.js, hide_reels.js, hide_stories.js, hide_pymk.js, hide_groups.js; adds feed_hydrate.js as always-on.

Sources: CajuM FlatBuffers https://cajum.github.io/fbgraphql/; AlterLab RelayPrefetchedStreamCache https://alterlab.io/blog/how-to-scrape-facebook-data-complete-guide-for-2026; dev.to/vhub data-ft https://dev.to/vhub_systems_ed5641f65d59/how-to-scrape-facebook-public-data-without-the-graph-api-in-2026-4ack. Compressed block (b7) for writeup-synthesis. Compressed block (b5) for Tier A1 (network-level GraphQL op-name filter).

notes.body: Phase 3 sources — (1) CajuM FlatBuffers decode pipeline https://cajum.github.io/fbgraphql/ — extracts `assets/graph_metadata.bin` from `com.facebook.katana.apk`, FlatBuffers-encoded, decoded via Python `CajuM/fb-graphql-schema` repo + flatc; emits every GraphQL type/field name; format survives 2019→2026; type names rotate but decode pipeline stable. (2) AlterLab RelayPrefetchedStreamCache pattern https://alterlab.io/blog/how-to-scrape-facebook-data-complete-guide-for-2026 — FB's initial GraphQL results embed in `<script type="application/json" data-content-len="…">` tags; payload path `data.require[i][0] === "RelayPrefetchedStreamCache"` → `req[3][1].__bbox.result.data`. Lets hide-toggle cosmetics run BEFORE React renders. (3) dev.to/vhub confirms mobile web still ships `data-ft` JSON with `mf_story_key` + sponsored flag in 2026: https://dev.to/vhub_systems_ed5641f65d59/how-to-scrape-facebook-public-data-without-the-graph-api-in-2026-4ack. (b7) writeup-synthesis consolidated all of these. (b5) for Tier A1 decision (network-level GraphQL op-name filter at shouldInterceptRequest). Acceptance criteria: after Phase 3, scroll-stops at ~9 entries reduced (because the MutationObserver storm is gone and feed cosmetics work at the data layer instead). The remaining scroll-stops will be addressed by Phase 6's IntersectionObserver rootMargin override. Migration timeline: Phase 3.1 is the ← CURRENT task when we begin implementation.

items.body: Build scripts/regenerate_gql_ops.py: CajuM FlatBuffers decode of com.facebook.katana.apk assets/graph_metadata.bin (extract APK via apktool d or unzip); emit app/src/main/res/raw/graphql_ops.json with authoritative op-name list. Use CajuM/fb-graphql-schema Python pipeline via flatc. Quarterly refresh cadence. Source: https://cajum.github.io/fbgraphql/

Build scripts/inspect_bundle.sh: capture HAR via desktop Chrome (mobile UA) on m.facebook.com, save HAR with content, pretty-print chunk sources via DevTools Sources {} button, grep output for `IntersectionObserver(`, `RelayPrefetchedStreamCache`, `fb_api_req_friendly_name`, `data-sigil` strings. Save to scripts/inspect_bundle_output.txt per capture.

Emit app/src/main/res/raw/selectors.json (canonical sigil/role names — `data-sigil="feed"` → `div[role="feed"]`, etc., plus all the hide_* targets) + app/src/main/res/raw/feed_schema.json (`data-ft` sponsored-flag field name + `mf_story_key` field name + ad-credit markers for current FB release). Source: https://dev.to/vhub_systems_ed5641f65d59/how-to-scrape-facebook-public-data-without-the-graph-api-in-2026-4ack
After step 3.3 emits the JSON files, run `pnpm gen-types` (Phase 2.4 task) to regenerate the .d.ts files consumed by feed_hydrate.ts and adblock-cosmetic.ts.

Build scripts/refresh_fb_metadata.sh as one-shot driver: redownload APK from Play Store CDN or via apktool d, decode graph_metadata.bin via regenerate_gql_ops.py, capture HAR via inspect_bundle.sh, diff selectors vs previous release's `selectors.json`, regenerate all res/raw/*.json, run gen-types, commit + tag release. Recommended quarterly cadence per (b6) — FB deploys ~weekly; canonical selectors rotate ~quarterly.

Extend ExternalRequestInterceptor.kt POST-body filter: parse `fb_api_req_friendly_name` from GraphQL POST bodies (read request body via WebResourceRequest; for POST we need shouldInterceptRequest withRequestBody access — use WebViewCompat.shouldInterceptRequest with a custom callback if standard shouldInterceptRequest lacks body access; alternative: use a custom URLRequest sniffer via a small Kotlin coroutine dispatcher); 404 anything not in graphql_ops.json allowlist (PolarisFeed, MBKNNotifications, Messaging, Profile). All other ops (StoriesToast, MarketplaceFeedSurface, ReelsHomeSurface, GamingSurface, Ads, Sponsored ops) get 404'd at the network layer per (b5) Tier A1.

Author app/src/main/ts/feed_hydrate.ts (compiled → res/raw/feed_hydrate.js; document_start injection): walk `<script type="application/json" data-content-len="…">` tags; find entry where `require[i][0] === "RelayPrefetchedStreamCache"`; descend to `req[3][1].__bbox.result.data`; mutate the data array per user toggles (removeAds drops items where `is_sponsored === 1`; hide_suggested/hide_reels/hide_stories/hide_pymk/hide_groups drop items matching selectors per `selectors.json`). Inject via `WebViewCompat.addDocumentStartJavaScriptCompat(view, '<script>', "*")` NOT the existing evaluateJavaScript (page-finished) call. Source: https://alterlab.io/blog/how-to-scrape-facebook-data-complete-guide-for-2026

Update MainViewModel.kt Script list (lines 42-53): remove Script entries for hide_suggested.js, hide_reels.js, hide_stories.js, hide_pymk.js, hide_groups.js (5 entries deleted). Add `Script(true, R.raw.feed_hydrate, "feed_hydrate.js")` as always-on (replace `Script(true, R.raw.scripts, "scripts.js")` with feed_hydrate as the always-on data-layer patcher; scripts.js becomes trimmed scripts.ts handling only the residual bridge protocols per Phase 4.4).

7d65839a.title: Phase 4 — Surviving DOM observer + CSS radix
7d65839a.description:
Authors the minimum surviving DOM observer + one-shot CSS injection bundle; trims scripts.ts to bridge protocols only.

Authors app/src/main/ts/adblock-cosmetic.ts (compiled → res/raw/adblock-cosmetic.js): single scoped MutationObserver on div[role=feed] subtree:true, requestAnimationFrame-debounced, data-nb-hidden early-bail (pattern already used at adblock.js:113 per (b2)). Reads selectors from selectors.json + sponsored-flag field name from feed_schema.json. Replaces 60+ lang-suffix sponsored-blocker with one-line JSON.parse(node.dataset.ft).<sponsored-flag> dispatch.

Authors app/src/main/ts/cosmetic.ts (one-shot, run on onPageFinished): emits <style id="nb-cosmetic"> with: global *, *::before, *::after, ::backdrop { animation: none !important; transition: none !important; scroll-behavior: auto !important; } (Tier A3); sticky_navbar rules; amoled_black rules; login-page download-button hide; tap-highlight color (-webkit-tap-highlight-color); loading-overlay restyle; desktop-mode third-button removal; user-select: text !important on feed-text elements (replaces scripts.js:181 span-scan).

Trims scripts.ts: DELETE banner watcher (scripts.js:40), third-child remover (scripts.js:100), text-select span-scan (scripts.js:181 — replaced by CSS user-select: text), loading-overlay restyle (scripts.js:197 — replaced by CSS), bottom-banner hide (scripts.js:217 — replaced by CSS). RETAIN: window.backHandlerNB() definition (scripts.js:120, called by NobookWV.kt:91 reading back "false"|"exit"|"scrolling"|"top"); settings-button re-injector + window.SettingsBridge?.onSettingsToggle?.() call (scripts.js:301); window.ThemeBridge?.onThemeColorChanged?.() notify (scripts.js:340 — converted to Phase 4.5 one-shot); _downloadBridgeInitialized guard + download-button initializer (scripts.js:350-357 wraps FileReader.readAsDataURL(blob) + DownloadBridge.downloadBase64File(reader.result, blob.type) to preserve FB session cookies).

Authors app/src/main/ts/theme_color.ts (one-shot on onPageFinished): document.querySelector('meta[name=theme-color]')?.content → window.ThemeBridge?.onThemeColorChanged(content ?? "null"). Replaces the perpetual watcher at scripts.js:340. Threads into existing native sysbar tint plumbing (ThemeChange.kt:10 → setThemeColor → MainViewModel → NobookWV.kt:140 → setWindow).

Audits copy_to_clipboard.ts for flexbox-order scrambling (Taprun 7-mechanism catalog). If confirmed, replaces textContent reads with RelayPrefetchedStreamCache.__bbox.result.data JSON .value field reads. Authors app/src/main/ts/lib/unscrambleByCssOrder.ts helper (10-line sort children by computed CSS order) as a fallback if hydration JSON isn't available.

Sources: compressed block (b2) for the root-cause body-subtree MutationObserver storm rationale; Taprun flexbox-order writeup https://taprun.dev/blog/facebook-anti-scraping-flexbox-order.html; compacted block (b7) codebase-discovery for scripts.ts survivors list (NobookWV.kt:91, scripts.js:120,301,340,350-357, jsBridge/NobookSettings.kt:9, jsBridge/ThemeChange.kt:10).

Decision rationale: backHandlerNB + SettingsBridge/ThemeBridge/DownloadBridge wiring are JS<->native contract protocols, not cosmetics — they stay as code (just typed in TS). The base64 download-bridge pattern at scripts.js:350-357 wraps FileReader.readAsDataURL inside the FB session, preserving cookies; native URL-only DownloadManager flow would lose them.

notes.body: Phase 4 sources — (b2) for the root-cause body-subtree MutationObserver storm rationale (8+ observers each doing full-document querySelectorAll on every mutation is the scroll-jank cause). Taprun flexbox-order writeup https://taprun.dev/blog/facebook-anti-scraping-flexbox-order.html (7-mechanism catalog; mechanism #3 is flexbox-order scrambling of single-char author-name spans). (b7) codebase-discovery for scripts.ts survivors list — NobookWV.kt:91 (backHandlerNB eval), scripts.js:120 (backHandlerNB def, called from NobookWV.kt:91), scripts.js:301 (SettingsBridge.onSettingsToggle call → opens native SettingsDialog via NobookSettings.kt:9), scripts.js:340 (ThemeBridge.onThemeColorChanged notify → setThemeColor via ThemeChange.kt:10), scripts.js:350-357 (_downloadBridgeInitialized guard + DownloadBridge.downloadBase64File call wrapping FileReader.readAsDataURL(blob) inside the FB session to preserve cookies). jsBridge/NobookSettings.kt:9, jsBridge/ThemeChange.kt:10, jsBridge/DownloadBridge.kt, jsBridge/ClipboardBridge.kt. Decision rationale: backHandlerNB + SettingsBridge/ThemeBridge/DownloadBridge wiring are JS↔native contract protocols, not cosmetics — they STAY as code (just typed in TS via bridges.d.ts). The base64 download-bridge pattern at scripts.js:350-357 wraps FileReader.readAsDataURL inside the FB session, preserving cookies; native URL-only DownloadManager flow would lose them (Phase 5.3/5.4 confirms this correction). Phase 4 MUST come after Phase 3 because cosmetic.ts's CSS rules reference selectors from `selectors.json` (Phase 3.3), and adblock-cosmetic.ts's one-line `JSON.parse(node.dataset.ft)` reference uses the sponsored-flag field name from `feed_schema.json` (Phase 3.3). Phase 4 items count = 6; Current task moves here after Phase 3 finishes.

items.body: Author app/src/main/ts/adblock-cosmetic.ts: single scoped MutationObserver on `div[role=feed] subtree:true`, requestAnimationFrame-debounced, `data-nb-hidden` early-bail (pattern already used at adblock.js:113 per (b2)). Reads selectors from `selectors.json` + sponsored-flag field name from `feed_schema.json`. Only this observer survives the cutdown (instead of the 8+ body-subtree observers per (b2)).

Replace 60+ lang-suffix sponsored-blocker in conventional code path with one-line `JSON.parse(node.dataset.ft).<sponsored-flag>` dispatch. 28a2b89d.title: Phase 5 — Native toggle migrations (KEEP base64 bridge pattern)
28a2b89d.description:
Migrates pinch_to_zoom and desktop_layout to native (zero-JS); KEEPS the existing base64 ClipboardBridge / DownloadBridge pattern (corrects the v1 plan which proposed native URL-only flows that would lose FB-session cookies). Adds image-resolution downgrade via ExternalRequestInterceptor. Optional NativeMediaViewerActivity.

Deletes pinch_to_zoom.ts; sets WebSettings.setBuiltInZoomControls(true) + setUseWideViewPort(true) in NobookWV.kt; INVERTS the gate in SettingsViewModel.kt (currently `!settings.pinchToZoom.value` per MainViewModel.kt:47, which iscounterintuitive — default behavior is to BLOCK pinch; the flip makes pinch enabled by default).

desktop_layout → ensures native setUserAgentString(DESKTOP_USER_AGENT) + setUseWideViewPort(true) path is in place (desktopUserAgent.kt:4-5 already provides the UA string constant).

KEEPS base64 `jsBridge/ClipboardBridge.kt` @JavascriptInterface copyImageToClipboard(base64) pattern — does NOT rewrite as native Android ActionMode/ClipboardManager URL-only flow. Rationale: the existing pattern at scripts.js wraps FileReader.readAsDataURL(blob) inside the WebView's FB session, preserving FB-session cookies in the blob fetch. Replacement with native URL fetch would either lose cookie auth or require plumbing CookieManager into the native request, which is much more code than the existing pattern. The bridge stays; only the script-side activation logic changes (move from a perpetual MutationObserver to a tap/context-menu handler).

KEEPS base64 `jsBridge/DownloadBridge.kt` @JavascriptInterface downloadBase64File(base64, mimeType) pattern — same rationale as above. The activation moves to a tap handler in download_content.ts; long-press → menu → "Download" path can additionally use Android's native ActionMode if we want a more native-feeling menu UI.

(Optional) Authors NativeMediaViewerActivity.kt: Compose full-screen image/video viewer. When image is tapped in the WebView, JS bridge passes the (already-authenticated) blob to native → display via Compose Image; save via DownloadManager for actual downloads.

Extends ExternalRequestInterceptor.kt for image-resolution downgrade (Tier B6): intercept FB image URLs (scontent-*.cdninstagram.com/...), allow only the smallest variant, 404 higher-res variants. Native media viewer loads full-res on tap via FB-session blob fetch via the existing bridge pattern.

Sources for KEEP-base64 decision: codebase-discovery via scripts.js:357, jsBridge/DownloadBridge.kt, jsBridge/ClipboardBridge.kt. Source for WebSettings docs: https://developer.android.com/reference/android/webkit/WebSettings#setBuiltInZoomControls(boolean). Source for image-res URL pattern: TBD via HAR inspection in Phase 3.2 (FB rotates stp= path params). Compressed block (b5) for Tier B6 image-resolution downgrade.

The base64 patterns are the right call. 7eb9db2b.title: Phase 6 — Aggressive feed prefetch (IntersectionObserver rootMargin override)

notes.body: Phase 6 sources — (b6) for the IntersectionObserver rootMargin override fix (m0041 — root cause: FB pager fires only when sentinel enters viewport with default rootMargin "0px"; user must wait for network round-trip at every page boundary; bigger rootMargin causes prefetch 2-3 screens ahead so by the time user reaches bottom, posts are already loaded). androidx.webkit addDocumentStartJavaScriptCompat: https://developer.android.com/reference/androidx/webkit/WebViewCompat. Trade-off: bigger rootMargin prefetches more aggressively → ~1.5× bandwidth burst on continuous scroll. Opt-in mitigates. Combined with (b2) observer cleanup gets near-seamless scroll because main-thread jank was delaying QPL timing marks that gate pagination. Acceptance criteria: zero scroll-jank observing FB's React-rendered feed on the user's specific hardware through ~30 entries of continuous fast scrolling, with aggressive-feeds toggle on.

items.body: Add opt-in setting "Aggressive feed prefetch" in SettingsViewModel.kt; default off (broadband cost ~1.5× on continuous scroll). User opts in via SettingsDialog checkbox.

Re-measure with JankStats (saved as `baselines/baseline_v2.txt`); compare to `baselines/baseline_v1.txt` from Phase 1.2; document deltas in `baselines/perf_report_v1.md`. Validate the reported "scroll-stop at ~9 entries" symptom is gone (target: seamless pagination to ~30+ entries before any hesitation).

Run full regression: verify each of the 13 user-facing toggles functions identically. Use `AdblockTest.kt` Playwright harness with refreshed selectors against live FB (assumes `refresh_fb_metadata.sh` has been run once and `generateAuth.kt` constants are filled via GH Actions secrets per Phase 7.4).

8af60769.description:

Documents refresh workflow in CONTRIBUTING.md: ≥3-monthly manual run of scripts/refresh_fb_metadata.sh against newest com.facebook.katana.apk. Step list: (a) pull newest FB APK from Play Store CDN or via apktool d, (b) run refresh_fb_metadata.sh (decodes graph_metadata.bin, captures HAR, diffs selectors vs previous, regenerates all res/raw/*.json), (c) `pnpm gen-types` to regenerate .d.ts, (d) `pnpm tsc --noEmit` to catch any TS-side drift, (e) commit + tag a minor release.

Adds hard rule in AGENTS.md / CONTRIBUTING.md: NEVER bypass the WebView for FB GraphQL. Native HTTP trips Meta's behavioral ML (multi-signal TLS/JA3 fingerprint + mouse/scroll velocity + time-on-page accumulated per session). Snapshot feeder in Phase 8, ad probes in Phase 3.7's graphql filter, and the inspection scripts in Phase 3.5 ALL must reuse the WebView session cookies or be a no-op. Sources: Clura https://clura.ai/blog/facebook-scraper (Python ~78% block rate, Playwright ~31%, real Chrome ~8%; WebView session inherits the human session).

Documents test commands in AGENTS.md: ./gradlew spotlessApply, ./gradlew detekt, ./gradlew compileDebugKotlin, ./gradlew lintDebug (ordered; NEVER ./gradlew qualityCheck — too expensive for incremental work). For TS work: `pnpm install && pnpm tsc --noEmit && pnpm bundleScripts` before pushing. Per project memory human rule #5.

Wires AdblockTest.kt harness to the refresh workflow: refresh_fb_metadata.sh regenerates selectors + auth.json; CI runs AdblockTest.kt against live FB with fresh selector JSON to catch selector decay between releases. Refills generateAuth.kt constants via GitHub Actions secrets (FACEBOOK_USERNAME, FACEBOOK_PASSWORD).

Note: project-memory human rule #5 says "For this Android project, do not call loader work complete unless the actual OpenCode patch path has been exercised: download/extract or otherwise use a real OpenCode linux-arm64 binary, run build.py to produce a patched binary, and try a runtime check such as patched-opencode --version." This rule is about the OpenCode loader project, NOT the Nobook fork — different project. Apply only the test-command-ordering part here.

Final QC: re-measures perf vs Phase 1 baseline; verifies no FB feature regression (reels button, stories, marketplace, profile navigation, composer open/close, reactions, comments, share sheet).

8cf70947.title: Phase 8 (Optional Tier-C Unlock) — Snapshot-feed-from-last-run
8cf70947.description:
DEFERRED. Only do this phase if Phase 1-7 finish and we want the additional cold-launch UX win. The RelayPrefetchedStreamCache pattern from (b7) AlterLab makes this concrete.

Persists RelayPrefetchedStreamCache.__bbox.result.data JSON to app/cache/feed_snapshot.json on successful feed onPageFinished. Adds a new SnapshotBridge.persistFeed(json: String) @JavascriptInterface in the existing base64/JSON bridge pattern style. The script-side (in feed_hydrate.ts) hands the parsed hydration JSON to native after every successful feed load.

On cold launch while the pre-warm WebView (Phase 1.6 WebViewInitializer.kt) navigates: reads the snapshot, renders native Compose feed cards. Author names from hydration JSON .value field (Taprun-safe — never textContent, which Flexbox-order-scrambles per Taprun 7-mechanism catalog). Post IDs from .mf_story_key. Single screen or two screens worth of cards (~5-8).

Fades-over from Compose to live WebView on onPageFinished of the warming WebView. Accepts ~3-5s staleness for the instant render. NEVER issues native HTTP fetch to FB for refresh (per the behavioral-ML rule from Phase 7.2 — Clura TLS/JA3 fingerprint + behavior patterns would block the request).

Sources: compacted block (b7) writeup-synthesis for the RelayPrefetchedStreamCache pattern from AlterLab https://alterlab.io/blog/how-to-scrape-facebook-data-complete-guide-for-2026. Taprun-safe rule for author-name JSON.value vs textContent https://taprun.dev/blog/facebook-anti-scraping-flexbox-order.html. Compressed block (b5) for the original Tier-C snapshot idea.

Decision rationale: persisting __bbox.result.data is a pure JSON read/write — no native HTTP request to FB. The WebView session is the only request path per behavioral-ML rule. Phase 8 is the high-leverage unlock on top of the Phase 1-7 foundation; was abstract in v1 plan, AlterLab pattern makes it concrete.

Acceptance criteria: cold-launch begins rendering native Compose feed cards in <100ms from app-process start; fades smoothly to live WebView when onPageFinished fires; no behavioral-ML alerts triggered on the user's normal account after a week of use.
